\chapter{At the Doctor}
\label{ch:hi-at-the-doctor}
\hlchaptermodality{107}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk to a doctor, find a hospital, say I am hurt or feel weak, and talk about health.}

Complete HI-C107-sehat: a visit to the doctor, from injury to health.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ḍākṭar]{\hi{डाक्टर} (ḍākṭar) — a doctor}

\label{lesson:HI-C107-doctor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for ill, then the Hindi for how one is feeling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{डाक्टर}}
\textbf{\hi{डाक्टर}} (\emph{ḍākṭar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a doctor\textquotedblright{}, English borrowed whole.

\textbf{\hi{डाक्टर} \hi{कहाँ} \hi{हैं}?} — \textquotedblleft{}where is the doctor?\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful plural \textbf{\hi{हैं}} for a person you are asking after.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The person to ask for.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍākṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ḍākṭar kahā̃ haiṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for ill, then the Hindi for how one is feeling, then say \emph{ḍākṭar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{डाक्टर} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A doctor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aspatāl]{\hi{अस्पताल} (aspatāl) — a hospital}

\label{lesson:HI-C107-aspatal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for how one is feeling, then the Hindi for a doctor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अस्पताल}}
\textbf{\hi{अस्पताल}} (\emph{aspatāl}) — \textquotedblleft{}a hospital\textquotedblright{}.

It is English \emph{hospital}, reshaped to fit Hindi sounds. \textbf{\hi{अस्पताल} \hi{कहाँ} \hi{है}?} — \textquotedblleft{}where is the hospital?\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A place to ask the way to when it matters.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aspatāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aspatāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{aspatāl kahā̃ hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for how one is feeling, then the Hindi for a doctor, then say \emph{aspatāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{अस्पताल} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hospital\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[coṭ]{\hi{चोट} (coṭ) — an injury, a hurt}

\label{lesson:HI-C107-chot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a doctor, then the Hindi for a hospital.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चोट}}
\textbf{\hi{चोट}} (\emph{coṭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}an injury, a hurt\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{चोट} \hi{लगी} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have been hurt\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a hurt has struck me\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to say you are hurt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{coṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{coṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe coṭ lagī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a doctor, then the Hindi for a hospital, then say \emph{coṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चोट} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An injury, a hurt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kamzorī]{\hi{कमज़ोरी} (kamzorī) — weakness}

\label{lesson:HI-C107-kamzori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a hospital, then the Hindi for an injury.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{कमज़ोरी}}
\textbf{\hi{कमज़ोरी}} (\emph{kamzorī}) — \textquotedblleft{}weakness\textquotedblright{}.

It opens on the \textbf{\hi{कम}} you know, \textquotedblleft{}little\textquotedblright{}: weakness is having little strength. \textbf{\hi{कमज़ोरी} \hi{लग} \hi{रही} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I feel weak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Weakness, built on a word you know.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamzorī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamzorī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kamzorī lag rahī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a hospital, then the Hindi for an injury, then say \emph{kamzorī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{कमज़ोरी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Weakness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sehat]{\hi{सेहत} (sehat) — health, fitness}

\label{lesson:HI-C107-sehat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an injury, then the Hindi for weakness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सेहत}}
\textbf{\hi{सेहत}} (\emph{sehat}) — \textquotedblleft{}health\textquotedblright{}, the long-term kind.

\textbf{\hi{तबीयत}} is how you feel today; \textbf{\hi{सेहत}} is how healthy you are. \textbf{\hi{सेहत} \hi{अच्छी} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}the health is good\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A doctor, a hospital, an injury, weakness, and health itself.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sehat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sehat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sehat acchī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an injury, then the Hindi for weakness, then say \emph{sehat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सेहत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Health, fitness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
